Prayesh Jain:

to the Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management Company Limited Q2 & H1FY27 earnings

Mr. Pradeep Sharma, Chief Financial Officer; and Mr. Paritosh Chittora, Head Investor

A. Balasubramanian: 
Thank you for hosting us and good evening everyone. Thank you for joining us on the Q2 & 
H1FY27 investors call. I hope you all had the opportunity to read through our earnings 
presentation which is available on both the stock exchanges and our company's website. 
 
Let me begin by sharing our perspective on the current macroeconomic environment. The 
global economy, as you know, demonstrated remarkable resilience in Q2 FY27. Growth 
sustained its momentum despite a challenging external environment. The prolonged 
geopolitical conflicts and inflationary pressures and El Niño and potential asset price 
corrections remain areas to watch, but the global growth outlook remains constructive. 
 
And India continues to stand out as one of the fastest-growing major economies powered by 
robust private consumption, resilient service sectors, and strong fixed-income and  fixed 
investment alongside a positive contribution from net exports, and growth momentum in the 
first half of the year came in well ahead of expectations. Government infrastructure spending 
and private capex and robust credit flows are sustaining investments. The IMF has revised its 
FY27 growth forecast for India from 6.4% to 7%, and the RBI revised its outlook upwards to 
7.1%, a reflection of confidence in the economic underlying strength. 
 
Economic activity has held firm even as we keep a close watch on the southwest monsoon and 
its implications for the upcoming Rabi season. In its October policy, the RBI raised the repo 
rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% and signaled a more cautious stance on inflation while 
reaffirming confidence in the growth trajectory. 
 
India's external position has been supported by healthy capital flows including NRI deposits, 
FCNR(B) balances, and forex reserves over US$ 730 billion. These strengthen our external 
sector resilience and provide a cushion in times of global uncertainty and related currency 
volatility. 
 
Moving to Indian markets, the quarter was marked by volatility amid elevated crude prices, 
high global bond yields, a weaker rupee, and shifting interest rate expectations. While  
large-cap indices corrected, the broader market held up relatively well reflecting confidence in

India's long-term growth story. Steady domestic participation through SIPs and continued 
financialization of household savings helped cushion the volatility and underscored the 
structural strength of India's capital market. 
 
A busy primary market reflected strong appetite among issuers and investors for capital 
formation, and looking ahead, near-term volatility may persist but earning growth and 
domestic investor base continue to provide a strong foundation for the longer-term outlook. 
 
Coming to an update on the Mutual Fund Industry, the quarterly average AUM stood at  
₹87.21 lakh crores as on 30th September 2026 compared to ₹77.13 lakh crores as of the same 
period last year, registering year-on-year growth of about 13%. The SIP contribution for the 
industry stood at ₹32,490 crores for September 2026, representing year-on-year growth of 
11%. The total mutual fund folios stood at 30 crores as on September 2026, growing by 17% 
year-on-year. 
 
During Q2 FY27, the industry saw total NFO collection of approximately ₹11,504 crores 
across asset classes with equity collection driven by index, aggressive hybrid, and value funds. 
Despite market volatility, the industry continued to witness healthy net inflows into equity-
oriented schemes reflecting investors' growing preferences for disciplined long-term investing. 
SIP flows remained resilient and retail participation stayed strong. Investor preferences 
continued to shift towards mid-cap, small-cap, and flexi-cap funds, a sign of confidence in 
India's long-term growth prospects and our participation broadening across market segments. 
 
Individual average AUM for September 2026 stood at ₹ 53.24 lakh crores contributing around 
61% of the total AUM. B30 cities with an average AUM of ₹16.37 lakh crores accounted for 
18.8% of total AUM, growing by 13% year-on-year. Deepening our reach in B30 is a strategic 
priority for us as this is where India's next chapter of wealth creation will come from. We are 
building our distribution network, digital capabilities, and investor engagement in these 
markets to be well placed to capture the opportunities ahead. 
 
Coming to the ABSLAMC performance highlights. At ABSLAMC, we are pleased to share 
that our overall average AUM, including alternate assets, which is EPFO mandate, crossed  
₹11 lakh crores milestones this quarter, and now stands at ₹11.06 lakh crores, a growth of 
140% year-on-year. This includes mandated money from ESIC and EPFO. Our mutual fund 
quarterly average AUM stood at ₹4.42 lakh crores, up by 4% year-on-year, and within this, 
our equity mutual fund quarterly average AUM stood at approximately ₹2.09 lakh crores, 
growing by 9% year-on-year. Our equity mix for the quarter stood at 47.4%. 
 
Our SIP contribution for September 2026 stood at ₹1,094 crores supported by 41.7 lakh folio 
contributing SIP accounts. Our total investors folio for September 2026 stood at 1.14 crores, 
up 6% year-on-year with the new SIP registration for the quarter at about 7.05 lakhs 
approximately. 
 
Our equity fund performance continues to be consistent. This has strengthened our investors' 
confidence and supported healthy inflows across flagship offerings like Flexi Cap, Balanced 
Advantage Fund, Multi-asset, and Small Cap Fund. In fact, our equity performance has now

distribution ecosystems.

both including fixed-income as well as equity assets under management, equity categories. 
These offerings are aligned with investors' demand for differentiated and specialized 
investment opportunities.

Opportunities Fund Series II, which focuses on senior secured lending opportunities in  
post-approval brownfield real estate projects across Tier 1 cities. 
 
At GIFT City, we have launched our retail fund offering enabling Indian and global investors 
to access inbound and outbound investment opportunities through a dedicated retail platform. 
Fundraising is underway for the ABSL Flexi Cap Fund which is for inward remittance. In the 
coming quarter, we plan to launch six funds across both retail and non-retail categories 
addressing inbound and outbound opportunities. Backed by a growing product suite and GIFT 
City global investment ecosystem, we are well placed to build a scalable offshore franchise in 
the coming years under the LRS scheme as well as for the global investors investing in India. 
 
Passives is one of the key anchors for our growth strategy, and we are committed to building 
a leadership position in this segment. In fact, we have introduced Birla Passives as a new brand, 
a dedicated brand, identify to strengthen our visibility to investors and distributors and drive 
higher mind share and grow market share. During the Q2 FY27, our passive quarterly average 
asset under management stood at approximately ₹39,860 crores, up 10% year-on-year. Our 
investor base continues to expand with the total folios reaching around 17.9 lakh folios.

₹241 crores in Q2 FY26.

compared to ₹1,072 crores in H1 FY26. Our H1 FY27 profit before tax is ₹702 crores as 
compared to ₹688 crores in H1 FY26. Our H1 FY27 profit after tax is ₹530 crores as compared 
to ₹518 crores in H1 FY26.
